s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution
salient_findings: Intensely pruritic skin lesions on anterior thighs
Lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and purpuric edges
Symmetric, mirror-image distribution on anterior thighs
key_facts: 6-year-old girl with no relevant medical history
Lesions resolve spontaneously without residual injury
No preceding infection, topical exposures, sunburn, bites, animal contacts, or recent medications
Laboratory studies are within normal limits

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, central clearing, and purpuric edges, matching the patient's skin lesions

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic targetoid morphology, although the patient's lesions lack typical target lesions

shortlist.label: Urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions, although the patient's lesions have a more fixed and annular morphology

shortlist.label: Annular erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to erythema annulare centrifugum, with annular morphology and possible purpuric edges, but less well-defined

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric edges and possible systemic involvement, although the patient's laboratory studies are within normal limits

raw.rationale: The patient's lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing, which is characteristic of Erythema annulare centrifugum. The lesions also occur in recurrent outbreaks and resolve spontaneously without residual injury, consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Erythema multiforme typically has a more acute onset and is often associated with systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Urticaria
rejected.why: Urticaria typically presents with wheals that are more transient and migratory, whereas the patient's lesions are well-defined and confluent with a more fixed pattern.

rejected.label: Annular erythema
rejected.why: While annular erythema shares some similarities with the patient's presentation, it is a broader term and Erythema annulare centrifugum is a more specific diagnosis that better fits the clinical description.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis typically presents with purpuric lesions and is often associated with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings, which are not present in this case.
